Enabling 40 Marketers for the AI Era

Stephanie Craig leads AI enablement for SAP SuccessFactors' HCM product marketing team. Her insight from PMA Seattle: structured knowledge beats better tools.

By Chris O'Hara · July 2026 · 5 min read

When you're responsible for enabling 40+ product marketers on AI, you learn quickly what actually moves the needle — and what's just noise.

Stephanie Craig

Global Director of Product Marketing, SAP SuccessFactors
AI Enablement Lead for HCM Marketing

Stephanie Craig is the Global Director of Product Marketing at SAP SuccessFactors, where she leads AI enablement for the company's HCM (Human Capital Management) product marketing team — more than 40 marketers spread across regions and product lines. She recently attended the Product Marketing Alliance summit in Seattle, looking for signals on what's working and what's hype.

What she came back with wasn't a list of new tools to try. It was a framework for thinking about what separates teams that are actually pulling ahead from teams that are just experimenting.

"If I had to say it simply: the tools are table stakes now. What separates the teams that pull ahead is whether their knowledge is structured enough to make those tools actually useful."
— Stephanie Craig

The Knowledge Structure Problem

Stephanie's insight cuts to the heart of a challenge many PMM teams are facing. Everyone has access to the same AI tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini. The differentiation isn't in the tool; it's in what you feed it.

For a team like SuccessFactors' HCM marketing org, that means having structured access to competitive intelligence, customer evidence, product positioning, and sales enablement content that's organized in a way AI can actually use. Without that foundation, you get generic outputs that sound like every other company in your category.

Insight 1

Tools Are Table Stakes

Every team has access to AI now. The competitive moat is in knowledge structure, not tool selection.

Insight 2

Enable, Don't Mandate

Forced adoption creates resistance. Show value through wins, then scale what works.

Insight 3

Centralize Knowledge

40+ marketers need consistent source materials. Federated content creates federated (inconsistent) outputs.

Insight 4

Quality In, Quality Out

AI amplifies whatever you feed it. Garbage positioning produces garbage content — just faster.

Voices from PMA Seattle

Stephanie flagged several speakers from the summit who reinforced her thinking on AI-augmented PMM:

Notable Speakers & Their Focus

  • Emily Johnson — Lighthouse
  • Kris Orlowski — Slack
  • Akshat Jain — TikTok
  • Kuber Sharma — UiPath
  • Kasturi Pal — Amazon Health
  • Sean Thomson — Gartner

The common thread across these sessions: the teams winning at AI aren't the ones with the most sophisticated tools. They're the ones who've done the hard work of structuring their market intelligence, positioning frameworks, and customer evidence in ways that make AI genuinely useful.

Scaling AI Enablement

Running AI enablement for 40+ marketers isn't the same as enabling a small team. Stephanie's approach focuses on building repeatable systems rather than one-off training sessions:

  • Central prompt libraries — curated prompts that embed SuccessFactors' positioning and voice
  • Shared context documents — market intelligence and competitive positioning that any marketer can reference
  • Win sharing — regular showcases of AI-assisted work that actually shipped
  • Governance guardrails — clear boundaries on what requires human review vs. what can ship directly

This is the work that doesn't show up in LinkedIn posts about AI productivity gains. It's not glamorous. But it's what determines whether a team's AI adoption produces real competitive advantage or just faster mediocrity.

The Bottom Line

Stephanie's takeaway is a reality check for PMM leaders chasing the latest AI release: the constraint isn't the tool — it's your knowledge structure.

If your competitive intelligence lives in scattered documents, your positioning is inconsistent across regions, and your customer evidence is buried in slide decks from 2023, no AI tool is going to save you. But if you've done the work to structure that knowledge — organized it, updated it, made it accessible — then AI becomes a genuine force multiplier.

That's the gap Stephanie is focused on closing for SuccessFactors. And it's a model worth studying for any PMM leader trying to enable a distributed team at scale.
